subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up & recommendation based on latency/throughput
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap + next steps

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key requirements you shared:
- Latency: 95th percentile target <= 100 ms for single-turn text generation (avg prompt ~40 tokens, responses up to ~200 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained peak of ~600–800 requests/sec during business hours; occasional bursts to ~1.2k rps for short windows.
- Data policy: customer PII excluded from logging; SOC 2 and contractual data controls required.
- Uptime/SLOs: mission-critical payment flows — want predictable latency and fallback behavior.

Initial recommendation (based on the call): Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) as primary for predictable latency and throughput, with Hosted API as burst/fallback for spikes and failover across regions.

Attachments: I attached an initial sizing workbook and a short one-pager on deployment options for your architecture team to review.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the sustained peak and burst numbers (600–800 sustained, 1.2k burst) and whether 512-token max responses are typical?
2) If confirmed, we’ll schedule a 30–45m sizing call with our infra team (Neha & Dev) to propose node counts / autoscale profile.
3) I’ll share a PO/contract checklist and SOC2 evidence while we size.

Available times: Mon/Tue mornings PT work best for Neha & Dev — do any of these slots work for you?

Thanks — Marissa

-- 
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Sustained peak: planning for ~750 rps (so your 600–800 range is accurate).
- Bursts: we see up to ~1.1k–1.3k rps for a few minutes (marketing pushes).
- Tokens: most responses are < 512 tokens, but occasionally we hit ~700 tokens for longer policy explanations.
- Latency target is firm at <=100 ms p95 for core payment verification flows; non-critical flows can tolerate higher latency.

Given that, we agree Dedicated sounds appropriate for the core flows. Two quick asks before the sizing call:
1) Can you outline what a 2-node vs 4-node Dedicated configuration looks like for our profile (cost ballpark + expected p95 latency)?
2) Do you support automatic regional failover / multi-region replication for KV cache + model routing?

We can do Tue 14 Jul at 09:30 PT for the sizing call.

–Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com | (206) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 06:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap + next steps

Alex — great, thanks for confirming and for the extra detail. Short answers here and we’ll go deeper on the sizing call (Tue 09:30 PT):

1) 2-node vs 4-node (ballpark):
- 2-node Dedicated (reserved pool): suitable for ~500–900 sustained rps depending on model and sequence lengths. Expected p95 latency for typical 512-token workloads: ~60–110 ms (varies by model variant & quantization). Monthly committed cost estimate: ~$45k–$70k depending on GPU type and reserved term.
- 4-node Dedicated: target for ~900–1.8k sustained rps with much lower p95 (we’d often be in ~40–80 ms p95 for same workload). Monthly committed cost estimate: ~$85k–$150k.

These are initial ranges — the sizing call will let us plug in your exact prompt/response length distribution and choose specific instance families (and whether mixed CPU/GPU caching helps). I’ve attached the sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) with a simple model we’ll fill during the call.

2) Regional failover: yes — our Dedicated offering supports multi-region routing and KV cache replication patterns. For synchronous KV use-cases we recommend active-active with eventual consistency for cache keys; for strict consistency we provide synchronous fallback routing to a regional instance with higher tail latency during failover windows. We’ll have Dev run through specifics on Tue.

Next steps for Tue 09:30 PT:
- Agenda: 1) Confirm token distribution & model variant; 2) Fill sizing workbook and pick node counts; 3) Review failover pattern and contract/PO timeline.
- Prep: If you can drop a sample of prompt/response lengths (anonymized), that will make outputs much tighter.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (summary). Also linking our SOC2 evidence page in the call notes.

See you Tue — Marissa

-- 
Marissa Cole
